remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required model-card disclosure for the exposed enterprise refund-workflow limitation has actually been prepared, reviewed, or attached to the certification packet.
The affected enterprise refund-workflow segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort because gating is random by workspace and does not exclude that use case.
The draft risk acceptance cannot satisfy the policy condition because it is unapproved and does not specifically address enterprise refund-workflow exposure.
Policy text states rollout controls, rollback, monitoring, and small initial percentage do not remove disclosure duties while the affected segment remains exposed.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor narrowed the claim in a reasonable way, but provided no new admissible evidence. That matters here because the missing item is not merely a presentation caveat; it is an unresolved compliance predicate. The admissible record supports general launch-readiness factors: aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and a reversible 4% rollout with rollback capability. The same record also shows the enterprise refund-workflow segment remains below target and remains exposed, the gate does not exclude it, the risk-acceptance draft is unapproved and non-specific, and policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. A caveated certification theory could be supportable only if there were evidence that the required disclosure was actually in the packet or otherwise completed as a launch condition. There is no such evidence here. So the Actor's reframing improves precision, but it does not convert the record to compliant_with_caveats. The support for certification remains incomplete on the present record.
